cohort: 543 infants (276 male, 277 female) attending the postnatal clinic of the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Enugu, Nigeria
finding: Compared to other studies, a smaller proportion of Nigerian neonates passed meconium in the first 24 hours, and several perinatal factors were associated with earlier first meconium passage, including term gestational age, birth weight ≥ 2.5kg, spontaneous vertex delivery, high Apgar score, and early commencement of breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery significantly affected the timing of first meconium passage (p<0.01).
gest_age: Mean gestational age at delivery was 38.8 weeks
followup_time: Median age at presentation was 42 days
